Definition: from Ἄρης (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of G4078; rock of Ares, a place in Athens:--Areopagus, Mars' Hill.
BiblicalUsage: The Areopagus, Mars' Hill, is the rock in Athens where the council sat, and Paul is brought there to explain his new teaching. He stands in the midst of Mars' Hill and speaks to the men of Athens about the unknown God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Areopagus is where the gospel met philosophy on its own ground, and Paul did not flinch, because the unknown God was not unknown to him.
